implementation_notes: On the server (Vapor), Leaf provides the pattern: #extend("base") copies a parent template in, the child declares regions with #export("content") ... #endexport and the parent pulls them with #import("content") (or renders its default body with #content), while #embed("sidebar", ["user": user]) renders a fragment in place with an optional context dictionary - that is the catalog's included view plus dynamic inclusion. Configure with app.views.use(.leaf), render with req.view.render("templateName", context). On Apple client platforms the same composition is SwiftUI's body/@ViewBuilder tree, a different mechanism; Leaf is the server-side answer.
pitfalls: #(...) escapes output but #raw(...) does not; treat raw output like any unescaped injection and keep user data out of it.
Leaf resolves templates through its renderer with caching enabled by default, so a missing #embed target or a stale template shows up at render time - warm up and invalidate deliberately.
The context passed to #embed is a [String: LeafData] dictionary: a renamed key degrades to a silent "no such key" render rather than a compile error, so keep the keys next to the fragment.
